confirmed_findings.summary: addTagToNote's CLOSED-note branch reports success (returns true, no banner) when composeUpdatedContent silently refuses the edit: on malformed frontmatter YAML composeFrontmatter's H1 branch (yamlDoc.ts:464) re-emits the original bytes without the new tag, and on a block-shaped `tags:` (block scalar / seq-of-maps) immutableBlockKeys (yamlDoc.ts:502) filters the key from both diff maps so the add is dropped. writeNote then writes byte-identical content, reindexNote confirms the unchanged disk, and line 7094 returns true. The OPEN-note twin was explicitly fixed (store.ts:1809-1825 reportSaveFailure when editNoteProps refuses); the closed branch never got the guard, and the 2026-08-01 inspection surfaced only the three OTHER exits (identity refusal, cascade gate, thrown write).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note synced from another device carries a YAML typo (stray tab / duplicated key — 'Map keys must be unique'). User right-clicks it (closed) in the file tree → Add tag → 'research'. readNote → parseFrontmatter's line-scanner fallback still projects a tags list → addTagToProps appends → composeUpdatedContent hits H1 and returns the original frontmatter verbatim → writeNote succeeds → addTagToNote returns true. In the batch multi-select path (line 10386) the note is counted as SUCCEEDED (failedTags not pushed), so a 40-note batch tag reports clean while N notes never received the tag. No error, no banner, index and disk agree with each other — only the user's belief diverges.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: addTagToNote's closed-note branch (+layout.svelte:7084-7094) has no compose-refusal guard — it writes composeUpdatedContent's output unconditionally and returns true. Both silent-drop mechanisms are real: (1) H1 (yamlDoc.ts:464) re-emits original bytes verbatim on YAML parse errors, and store.parseFrontmatter's line-scanner fallback (store.ts:2683-2689) still projects a tags property from unparseable YAML, so addTagToProps produces a diff the composer then discards; (2) immutableBlockKeys (yamlDoc.ts:298-302, applied at 502-508) filters a block-shaped tags key from BOTH diff maps, dropping the add, while parseFrontmatter projects it as an editable-looking nested-map row that addTagToProps mutates without any type check. writeNote then persists byte-identical content, reindexNote confirms the unchanged disk, line 7094 returns true — no banner, no error. The asymmetry is confirmed: the OPEN-note twin got exactly this guard in store.ts:1814-1824 (PJ-207 §15, reportSaveFailure on editNoteProps refusal, with a comment naming addTagToNote as the caller that "used to be told the save succeeded"), and frontmatterIsRewritable (yamlDoc.ts:419) exists for this exact question but is never called on the closed path. Batch amplification confirmed at +layout.svelte:10386: a true return keeps the note out of failedTags, so a multi-note batch reports clean while notes silently never received the tag. No refutation applies: the write is awaited but carries unchanged bytes; nothing surfaces the refusal; index and disk agree so no reconcile will ever flag it.

confirmed_findings.summary: addLinkToNote's CLOSED-note branch has the identical unguarded exit: composeUpdatedContent on a note whose frontmatter YAML is malformed returns the original content (H1), the typed-link frontmatter property is silently dropped, writeNote succeeds, the background reindex derives no note_links row from the unchanged disk — and the caller's Reviewer UI 'updates optimistically (refreshAfterConnect)' per the comment at line 1568, so the connect is SHOWN as made.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User connects note A to note B ('supports') from the Reviewer while A is not open in any tab, and A's frontmatter has a parse error. addTypedLinkToProps appends the supports: [[B]] list to the projection; composeFrontmatter sees doc.errors and passes the original bytes through; the write lands byte-identical; reindexNote finds no new edge. The Reviewer shows the Living Link as created; A leaves the orphan lens optimistically. The link exists nowhere — not in the .md, not in note_links — and nothing ever reports it. On the OPEN path the same condition raises the save-health banner (saveTabContent:1814-1825); closed notes fail silently.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in code: addLinkToNote's CLOSED branch (store.ts:1544-1570) has no frontmatterIsRewritable guard. On a closed note with malformed frontmatter YAML: parseFrontmatter falls back to its line scanner without throwing (store.ts:2559-2561 comment confirms), addTypedLinkToProps returns a non-null projection, and composeFrontmatter's H1 branch (yamlDoc.ts:464) passes the original frontmatter bytes through verbatim — with the body unchanged, the writeNote at store.ts:1562 writes byte-identical content and succeeds. The background reindexNote (store.ts:1569) indexes unchanged content, deriving no note_links row; its .catch never fires. The caller chain then reports success: RelatedCandidates.choose (RelatedCandidates.svelte:145-152) optimistically removes the candidate and fires onConnected, and ReviewerView.refreshAfterConnect (ReviewerView.svelte:249-254) drops the note from the orphan/fragile lens. The typed link exists nowhere — not on disk, not in the index — and nothing surfaces it, not even a console line. The OPEN path surfaces this exact condition via reportSaveFailure (store.ts:1814-1825), whose comment explicitly names addLinkToNote as a caller that 'used to be told the save succeeded' — proving the closed branch is the missed parity site of the PJ-207 §15 fix. Reachable by design: the Reviewer's orphan lens surfaces closed notes, and malformed-YAML notes are the exact population the open-path refusal machinery was built for. Not APP-KILLER: no pre-existing content is lost or corrupted; the silent loss is the user's just-made connect act, and the note re-enters the lens on the next Reviewer load (unexplained, but re-discoverable).

confirmed_findings.summary: On a note whose content starts with '---' but has no closing '\n---' fence (e.g. a body that opens with a markdown horizontal rule, or a truncated frontmatter block), rewrite_frontmatter_sources hits the 'Malformed frontmatter — leave alone' branch and returns the content UNCHANGED — but rewrite_note_sources_on_disk (line 717-731) still returns `effective = recognised(&ids)` as if the write landed, and sources_set_manual (line 817-829) then mirrors those ids into note_meta.sources, clears the pending suggestion row, and returns Ok(()). The identical twin exists for the vertical axis at line 1160 (rewrite_frontmatter_content_type) feeding content_type_set_manual.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User's note begins with '---' as a thematic break with no second fence (or a crash-truncated frontmatter). The note has no sources, so the background scan queues a suggestion. User clicks Accept in the Source Review panel → sources_set_manual/content_type_set_manual return Ok, the card disappears, note_meta.sources/content_type now hold the accepted ids — but the .md on disk was never touched. The next reindex of that note (index_note at search.rs:8037/8047 re-derives both columns from disk) silently reverts the mirror to NULL: the user's Accept evaporates with no error anywhere, and until that reindex the index is silently divergent from disk. The scan will later re-propose the same suggestion, so the user can accept the same card forever and it never sticks.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: fence_offset (sources/mod.rs:342) accepts any content trim-starting with "---" (including a thematic-break opener or truncated frontmatter), and when no "\n---" exists anywhere later, rewrite_frontmatter_sources:550-553 silently returns content unchanged. rewrite_note_sources_on_disk:717-731 still returns effective=recognised(input ids) with no rewritten-vs-original comparison, so sources_set_manual:817-829 mirrors the never-written ids into note_meta.sources, clears the pending suggestion, and returns Ok(()) — the Accept card disappears and sources_get_for_note (mirror-only read, :754) confirms the phantom values. index_note (search.rs:8037/8047) re-derives both columns from disk via extract_sources/extract_content_type, whose extract_axis_values_raw (:243-245) returns empty for the same malformed shape, so the next reindex silently reverts the mirror to NULL: the user's Accept (or PropertyEditor exact-set — same branch, merge:false) evaporates with no error anywhere, and the same suggestion can be re-proposed and re-accepted indefinitely. Twin confirmed verbatim for content_type at :1160-1162 feeding content_type_set_manual. No guard, no surfaced error, no visible self-correction — false-success plus a real index-disk divergence window. Not APP-KILLER: note body content is never corrupted (the branch deliberately leaves it alone); the loss is the classification action, not knowledge content.

confirmed_findings.summary: The merge-view rebuild $effect launches async build() (awaits readNote of the .conflict sidecar + dynamic import of @codemirror/merge) with no generation/seq token and no cancellation; destroyView() cannot revoke an in-flight build, so a superseded build for note A can resolve LAST and assign mergeView = A's panes while target already points to note B. saveMerged() reads current target (B) but stale mergeView (A).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Two .conflict sidecars exist (normal after a sync pull). User clicks Merge on conflict A; while build(A) is parked on the sidecar readNote / first-time chunk import, user clicks Cancel, then Merge on conflict B. build(B) completes and renders; build(A) then resolves, appends its panes into B's overlay and overwrites the module-level mergeView. User clicks 'Save merged': resolveConflictMerge(B.notePath, B.sidecarPath, A_yourText) durably writes note A's composed content into note B's .md through the model and marks B's conflict resolved — note B's own content and its conflict copy's resolution are silently replaced with another note's text. No error, save reports success. (Also: the superseded MergeView's two EditorViews are never .destroy()ed — Rule 4 leak.) Sibling code in this codebase (epGeneration, scGeneration, BaseTab lastRun) guards exactly this shape; this component has no guard.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in src/lib/components/ConflictMergeView.svelte (lines 93–150): build() has two real suspension points (await readNote of the .conflict sidecar — a Tauri invoke — then await import('@codemirror/merge')) with no generation token and no post-await staleness check; destroyView() can only destroy the currently-assigned mergeView, never an in-flight build, so a superseded build(A) that resolves after build(B) appends A's panes into the live mount and overwrites the module-level mergeView. The trigger sequence (Merge A → Cancel → Merge B) is the only physical path — the banner z-index 99999 sits under the overlay z-index 100000 — and it is self-selecting: the race needs build(A) slow, and a slow build showing the loading state is exactly what makes the user cancel and switch to conflict B (slow sidecar reads are the code's own documented environment: AV/sync tools holding freshly-written files during a sync pull, which is also when multiple sidecars exist). In the parked-at-readNote interleaving, build(B) renders first and fills the visible area (its view is child 1 at height:100%, A's late panes land below the fold), so the screen shows note B correctly while mergeView points to A; saveMerged() then reads mergeView.a (A's text) and resolveConflictMerge(B.notePath, B.sidecarPath, A_text) (store.ts:6157) pushes A's content into B's model, durably writes it to B's .md, reindexes, trashes B's sidecar, and reports success — silent cross-note content replacement with the conflict marked resolved. The mirror interleaving silently discards the user's visible merge edits and resolves B unreviewed; every interleaving also leaks the superseded MergeView's two EditorViews (never destroyed). No guard, freeze, reconcile, or error surface interrupts any of this. HIGH rather than APP-KILLER because the window requires two simultaneous conflicts plus slow sidecar IO plus a cancel-and-switch inside that window — narrow, but real and made likelier by the very slowness that opens it. Fix: a buildGen token checked after each await (bail and destroy the just-built instance when stale), the epGeneration/scGeneration pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase.

confirmed_findings.summary: The cross-volume/fallback folder-trash copy+remove serializes only on the FOLDER's path lock, but editor saves lock per-FILE paths — a debounced save to a note inside the folder lands between that file's copy and remove_dir_all and is silently destroyed; the in-code comment (8597-8600) claims this exact race 'now serializes', which is true only for single-file trashes.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User has a dirty note open inside folder F (debounced save pending, >=1.5s). They delete F in 'trash' mode. gate_rename of F into .trash fails for a non-collision reason — e.g. OneDrive/AV holding a handle on a descendant exhausts the 5 retries, or the trash root is on another volume — so move_into_trash_folder falls back to with_path_lock(F){ copy_dir_recursive(F, dest); remove_dir_all(F) }. with_path_lock keys on F's path; the editor's gate_write keys on F/note.md — different lock keys, no serialization. copy_dir_recursive copies note.md (pre-save bytes), the debounced save then writes the final keystrokes into F/note.md successfully (parent still exists mid-copy), and remove_dir_all destroys it. delete_path returns Ok; the .trash copy silently lacks the last edits; nothing anywhere records that a write landed inside the doomed tree.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: the lock registry (write_gate.rs:124-142) is exact-path keyed with no ancestor/prefix awareness, so with_path_lock(F) at libraries.rs:8607 and an editor save's gate_write(F/note.md) take DIFFERENT mutexes — the 8597-8600 comment's "now it serializes" is true only for single-file trashes, false for folders. The fallback is reachable (trash_move_decolliding returns NotRenamed for any non-collision gate_rename failure: retry-exhausted AV/sync/Explorer directory-handle ACCESS_DENIED, or cross-device on a pre-MIG-108 universe with an external library — the docstring's own named expected case). A descendant write landing between copy_dir_recursive and remove_dir_all succeeds (parent exists mid-copy), is then destroyed by remove_dir_all, delete_path returns Ok, the .trash copy lacks the edits, the journal even records a SUCCESSFUL write, and deleteWithSetting then wipes the write-ahead net and disposes the model — silent, unrecoverable. One correction to the recipe: the candidate's exact "debounced save pending at click time" is largely drained by preserveWorkBeforeVacating (store.ts:5099, awaited flush of dirty tabs under F before delete_path). But the class survives concretely: (1) tabs stay open/editable during the ENTIRE delete_path execution (teardown runs after the await), so keystrokes during the multi-second fallback window (retries + recursive copy of a large folder) arm a fresh 1.5s debounced save that lands mid-window; (2) a second-window edit of a note in F is invisible to the main window's flush (separate webview, own stores) and saves via its own write_note straight into the window; (3) cascade gate_rmw rewrites of F's descendants likewise key per-file.

confirmed_findings.summary: The detached rename/move/folder-rename DB tails re-acquire SearchState.db AFTER detachment with no universe-generation check: a universe switch between the command's ensure_search_db_ready and the tail's lock acquisition either silently skips migrate_note_db_paths (conn None, no diag_log in that arm) or hands the tail the NEW universe's connection, where the 'rename' alias INSERT (1865-1868) plants a foreign-path, empty-cid row into the wrong universe's note_aliases (no FK to stop it — verified schema search.rs:5469).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User renames note A while a long writer (reindex_library, cascade reindex loop) holds SearchState.db — rename_item returns Ok and its spawn_blocking tail parks at state.db.lock() (libraries.rs:1853). User switches universe during the park. (a) invalidate_search_state nulls state.db first: the tail's `if let Some(conn)` arm is skipped with NO log line for the migrate — all 11 path-bearing tables in the departing universe keep the dead old path (search/backlinks/review serve a path that no longer exists) until that universe's next boot reconcile; the [rename-tail] START/END lines still appear, so the log reads clean. (b) The new universe's init completes first: guard is Some(NEW conn) — migrate no-ops (src_exists guard), but the `let _ = conn.execute(INSERT OR IGNORE INTO note_aliases …)` runs against the NEW universe's DB, inserting alias_lower=old-title → path-in-the-other-universe with cid_cn='' — a durable garbage row that the new universe's alias resolution can serve for that title. Same conn-None silent-skip arms exist per-chunk in rename_folder_db_tail (1935) and move_item_db_tail (2764), where a mid-loop switch strands part of a folder's descendants unmigrated with no log.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: all three detached tails (rename_item_db_tail libraries.rs:1852, rename_folder_db_tail :1935 per-chunk, move tail) re-acquire SearchState.db after detachment with no federation_generation check, while invalidate_search_state (search.rs:11228) nulls state.db on every universe switch — violating the codebase's own Architect Invariant 10, which reconcile.rs:270-288 records as a prior PJ-207 §8 HIGH finding fixed in the boot reconcile but left unfixed in these tails. Arm (a) is real: the conn==None arm silently skips migrate_note_db_paths with no log line while [rename-tail] START/END still print — but it is self-healing, not durable loss: at the departed universe's next activation the boot reconcile relocates the dead row by cid_cn via migrate_note_db_paths, preserving review/link/alias aux data (test at reconcile.rs:865-871), and logs the heal. Arm (b) is real and durable: note_aliases.cid_cn exists (ALTER search.rs:4131), the INSERT succeeds against the new universe's DB, and nothing ever cleans it (reconcile heals only note_meta and `continue`s on out-of-root rows at reconcile.rs:345-356) — though consequence is blunted because the only alias→path resolver (libraries.rs:3153-3155) filters candidates by path_under_library + exists, and other consumers filter by source or path-join. Additionally worse than stated: rename_folder_db_tail loads libraries ONCE at tail start (:1911), so a mid-tail switch lets its reindex loop pass the stale-library check and reindex_single_note (search.rs:12688, no ownership re-check) plants foreign-path note_meta/FTS/sky rows into the NEW universe's DB — rows reconcile skips forever (counted in the drift notice only when the universes are federated). Severity stays MED, not HIGH: the .md files are never touched, the departed universe self-heals with earned data preserved, the durable residue is inert-by-guards or additive contamination rather than knowledge loss, and the window requires a long writer plus a universe switch during the park.

confirmed_findings.summary: commitFocusSave (the Focus-mode save path, origin 'focus_pane') durably writes the body and reindexes but NEVER calls reembedNote — it is a fifth body-changing save path the PJ-207 §15 swallowed-embed fix missed (it wired only handleSave, handleFlush, navFlushEnv, and the prop-save runPostSave).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Semantic search enabled. User opens a note, enters Focus mode, rewrites the body substantially, exits (or the 1500ms debounce fires). commitFocusSave's onSaved runs broadcast + reindexNote only. note_embeddings keeps the pre-edit vector with no self-heal: per store.ts:4149-4154, the boot backfill only embeds notes with NO embedding row, index_repair.rs never touches note_embeddings, and constellation_search_reindex does not re-embed. Semantic search, 'similar notes', and CECE answer from the pre-edit vector forever — no error, no banner, nothing logged. A user who works primarily in Focus mode accumulates a silently stale semantic index across their whole corpus.
confirmed_findings.reason: commitFocusSave (+layout.svelte:1769-1798) is a real fifth body-changing save path whose onSaved does only broadcast + reindexNote — no reembedNote — while the PJ-207 §15 fix's own doc comment (store.ts:4145-4147) and grep confirm the embed choke point was wired to exactly four sites (NoteEditor handleSave/handleFlush, navFlushEnv, prop-save runPostSave). No self-heal exists: constellation_embed_notes with force=false (embeddings.rs:446-457) skips any note that already HAS an embedding row via a pure existence check (no content comparison), so the boot backfill never refreshes a stale vector; constellation_search_reindex does not embed; and the focus save marks the model clean, so flushOutgoing/navFlushEnv (store.ts:690) never fires afterward. The failure is silent — embedHealthError surfaces only a FAILED reembedNote call, and here the call is never made. Concrete repro: semantic search on, edit a note's body in Focus mode, let the 1500 ms debounce or exit-flush fire; disk and FTS update but note_embeddings keeps the pre-edit vector permanently, so semantic search / similar notes / CECE answer from stale content with no error. Heals only if the user later re-edits that note in NotePane — a Focus-primary workflow accumulates corpus-wide stale vectors.

confirmed_findings.summary: retrySaveFailure's onSaved reindexes but never calls reembedNote (and never broadcasts screen:note-saved) — yet for a note whose original editor_save FAILED, this retry is the ONLY save that ever lands, so the embed opportunity is lost permanently.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note's file is transiently locked (antivirus/sync tool); the debounced editor_save write fails → handleSave's onSaved (which carries the reembedNote) never runs → save-health banner appears → the ~10s auto-retry (or the Retry button) calls retrySaveFailure, which succeeds and clears the banner. The user sees success. The lexical index is current, but the note's vector stays at its pre-edit text with no retry path and no message (same no-self-heal chain as store.ts:4149-4154). An open second-screen copy is also never told (no broadcastNoteSaved), showing stale content until an unrelated event.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: retrySaveFailure (store.ts:520-531) is a real durable-save site whose onSaved runs only reindexNote — no reembedNote, no broadcastNoteSaved — while the editor_save path it substitutes for (NoteEditor.svelte:316-339) does broadcast + reindex + reembed + CECE. On a transient write failure the original save's onSaved never runs, the model stays dirty, and the ~10s auto-retry (+layout.svelte:1761-1767) or banner Retry lands the ONLY successful save for that edit, marks the model clean, and clears the banner (user sees full success). No self-heal exists: the boot backfill calls constellation_embed_notes without force and the Rust side (embeddings.rs:446-457) skips any note that already has a note_embeddings row (no freshness column); constellation_search_reindex does not re-embed; index_repair.rs never touches note_embeddings; embedHealthError never fires because the embed was never attempted. All dirty-gated flush paths are inert once the retry cleaned the model. Result: semantic search / similar-notes / CECE serve the pre-edit vector permanently for an untouched note, silently — the exact divergence class PJ-207 §15 fixed at the four other save sites, with retrySaveFailure the missed fifth. The absent broadcast also leaves an open second-screen copy on pre-edit content with no refresh event.

confirmed_findings.summary: resolveConflictMerge ('merge_resolve') durably writes the user's hand-merged BODY and reindexes, but never calls reembedNote — the merged text is a body change on the exact class of path PJ-207 §15 ruled must re-embed.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: An external edit conflicts with dirty local edits → .conflict sidecar + banner → the user merges in the two-pane merge view and resolves. The merged content (typically containing text from BOTH versions, differing substantially from what was last embedded) is written durably and reindexed, the sidecar is trashed, everything reports success. note_embeddings keeps the pre-merge vector permanently (no self-heal — store.ts:4149-4154), so semantic search / similar-notes / CECE silently answer from content that no longer exists on disk.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: resolveConflictMerge's onSaved (store.ts:6180-6183) fires only emit + reindexNote — no reembedNote — and standardSaveEnv adds no embed of its own. Every other body-writing durable-save site (NoteEditor:329/:445, navFlushEnv:660, prop-save runPostSave:1875) got the PJ-207 §15 reembedNote call; the merge resolve is a fifth such site that was missed, and the one where the body change is guaranteed substantial (merged text contains never-embedded external content). No self-heal exists: constellation_embed_notes force=false skips on row EXISTENCE only (embeddings.rs:446-457, no content hash), reindex_single_note never embeds, reconcile.rs only relocates the stale row, markRecentWrite (store.ts:6173) suppresses the watcher echo, and the post-merge model is clean so no later autosave fires. embedHealthError is never set — the flow reports full success (sidecar trashed, banner dismissed). With Semantic Search enabled (real user toggle, enabledFeatures.semanticSearch), the merged note's note_embeddings vector stays frozen at pre-merge text indefinitely — semantic search / similar-notes / CECE silently answer from content no longer on disk — until the user happens to body-edit that note again.

confirmed_findings.summary: restoreSessionTabs dedups restored tabs against live tabs by RAW path string (have.has(b.path)) while every sibling dedup surface (openNoteTab :3263, loadTabHistoryEntry :2011, adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs :1297) normalizes separators via normPath — a mixed-separator pairing slips past and mints a SECOND tab + SECOND independent NoteModel for one file, the exact B1 two-writers-last-wins clobber those fixes closed. The intra-snapshot dedup (seen.has(saved.path), :3757) and activeTabPath match (:3834) are raw too, so once duplicated the session snapshot persists BOTH forms and every subsequent boot silently restores the two-model state.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Session snapshot holds note X under 'E:/U/note.md' (stored from a wikilink-resolved tab path). At next boot, during restoreSessionTabs' multi-second awaited resolveNoteContent reads, the user clicks the same note in the file tree — openNoteTab mints a tab at the Rust-canonical 'E:\U\note.md' (restore's built tabs are not yet committed, so its dedup can't see them). The restore's one-commit dedup then raw-compares 'E:/U/note.md' against 'E:\U\note.md', misses, and appends a second tab + openNoteModel — two independent models for one file. The user types a paragraph in tab A (debounced save lands it on disk), later types in stale-seeded tab B; B's save composes its pre-A body and durably overwrites A's paragraph. Each window's own write is echo/recentWrite-suppressed and both models are self-consistent (clean, baseline = own write), so no conflict sidecar, no banner, no journal anomaly — the paragraph is gone from disk with nothing to say so. The session tracker then snapshots both path forms, so the two-model exposure survives every restart.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: restoreSessionTabs' one-commit dedup (store.ts:3806) compares RAW path strings while its own comment claims "same discipline as openNoteTab" — but openNoteTab (:3263) normalizes separators, a fix the 2026-08-01 inspection added expressly because mixed-separator stored Windows paths are real and were minting duplicate tab+model pairs. The session snapshot stores tab.path verbatim (session.ts:106), the restore runs fire-and-forget with the UI live, and its comment (:3800) acknowledges user opens DURING the awaited reads — those opens commit first, openNoteTab's dedup cannot see restore's uncommitted tabs, and restore's raw dedup then misses across forms, appending a second tab + second independent NoteModel (models keyed by tab id, no path guard). No downstream defense: the app's own editor saves are watcher-suppressed at the write gate and announce_disk_write fires only for template/sources writes, so neither model ever adopts the other's save; write_note has no base check; no sidecar/banner can fire. Typing in both tabs is the exact B1 last-writer-wins durable clobber with no surfaced error. The intra-snapshot dedup (:3757) and activeTabPath match (:3834) are raw too, so once duplicated both path forms persist in session.json and the two-model state is recreated every boot with no race needed. Severity stays MED (not APP-KILLER): the initial trigger needs a narrow confluence (a differing-form stored path AND a user open of that exact note inside the restore window), and the duplicate tab is at least visible in the tab bar — but the data loss itself is silent, durable, and self-perpetuating.

confirmed_findings.summary: closeTab awaits flushOutgoing but ignores its FlushResult, then disposes the model (closeNoteModel:3869); a 'still_dirty' outcome (flushIfDirty's bounded 4-pass loop exhausted, noteSession.ts:306) leaves the residual keystrokes only in the model, which is then deleted with no net and no surface. The closeTab comment claims 'the write-ahead net + save-health banner preserve a failed write' — true for reason='write_failed' (setNet retained) and for 'cascading' (explicit stash at store.ts:711), but NOT for 'still_dirty': the last successful save's clearNetIf wiped the net (its content matched its own write), and the newer-than-last-write keystrokes were never netted.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User is mid typing burst and closes the tab via keyboard (focus stays in the CM6 editor, which remains mounted during the awaited flush) on a folder where each disk write is slow (AV-scanned/synced — PJ-207 itself calls >1500ms writes 'ordinary'). A keystroke lands during each of the 4 flush write windows, so flushIfDirty exits with dirty content newer than the 4th durable write and returns {ok:false,'still_dirty'}. closeTab proceeds: closeNoteModel deletes the model holding the final keystrokes; NotePane's teardown doFlush then hits compose→no_model and early-returns BEFORE its setWriteAhead line (NoteEditor.svelte:379), so nothing is netted. The last ~1-2s of typed text is gone from disk, net, and screen with no banner, no journal marker, no error.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: closeTab (store.ts:3853) awaits flushOutgoing but ignores the FlushResult and disposes the model at 3869. For reason='still_dirty' (flushIfDirty's MAX=4 loop exhausted, noteSession.ts:301-306) the residual keystrokes are unprotected: each successful pass's clearNetIf (noteSession.ts:271, store.ts:390-394) wipes the net because the mid-write keystroke reaches only the model (NoteEditor.svelte:803 onDocChange→editBody), never the net; still_dirty returns without calling onError, so no save-health banner. The cascading branch stashes to the net (store.ts:709-712) and write_failed retains the net + banners — still_dirty alone gets neither. Post-disposal rescue is impossible: the teardown flush's compose returns no_model (noteModel.ts:530-531) and early-returns at NoteEditor.svelte:379 BEFORE the setWriteAhead at 427; a late debounced save hits the same no_model refusal (noteSession.ts:253-254). NAV_FLUSH_ENABLED=true (store.ts:263). Reachable: 4 consecutive slow-but-successful writes (the codebase itself calls >1500ms writes ordinary on AV-scanned/synced folders, NoteEditor.svelte:300-302) while the user keeps typing into the still-mounted, still-focused editor — plausible because the tab visibly stays open during the awaited flush. Loss is silent (no banner, no journal marker, tab closes normally) but bounded to the keystrokes typed after the 4th compose (~the last 1-2s of typing); everything earlier is durably written. confirmed_findings.summary: reloadTabsFromDisk matches walker-reported rewritten paths to open tabs with raw string equality (t.path === fp at 1106, byPath.get(t.path) at 1139/1161) — no case folding, no NFC folding, no separator normalization — while every sibling comparator in the same flow folds exactly these (PJ-092 belt at +layout.svelte:7495 NFC+normPathLC 'the exact Arabic-root form normPathLC alone can't fold'; Rust path_identity_key at libraries.rs:6753 canonicalize+NFC+lowercase; focusPathAmong at store.ts:1076 lowercases because 'Windows will happily hand back either casing'). The two compared sources are cross-origin: t.path from tree/session/resolution, fp from note_meta rows or the disk walk.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: An Arabic-titled referrer's open tab carries an NFD (or differently-cased) form of the path while note_meta / the walk reports the NFC (or other-cased) form — the divergence class the PJ-092 belt was explicitly built for. The walker rewrites [[Old]]→[[New]] on disk; reloadTabsFromDisk's exact match finds no tab: no adopt, no {#key} remount, no refusal, no conflict — the path silently falls out of `targets`. The clean on-screen model keeps the pre-cascade body; minutes later the user edits that note and the debounced save composes the full body from the stale model, writing [[Old]] back over the walker's rewrite. The cascade result for that referrer is silently reverted on disk, the index is then reindexed to match the reverted disk, and no surface ever reports it.
confirmed_findings.reason: The raw t.path === fp match at store.ts:1106 (and the raw byPath.get(t.path) lookups at 1139/1161) is the single un-folded comparator in a pipeline whose every other stage folds exactly the divergences at issue — and those foldings were added as fixes for OBSERVED Windows misses, per the code's own comments: focusPathAmong in this same function folds case+slash ("Windows will happily hand back either casing"), the sibling adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs was fixed 2026-08-01 because a raw lookup "made every Windows tab miss, silently disabling the whole external-adopt/conflict arbitration", openNoteTab's dedup normalizes because "a mixed-separator stored path must not slip past dedup", resolve_wikilink_cross_library documents that strict == "drops to '' on Windows slash / trailing-slash / case drift" (and its ResolvedLink.path is what a wikilink-opened tab stores), and the cascade's own exclusion path uses canonicalize+NFC+lowercase (path_identity_key) plus the NFC+normPathLC PJ-092 belt because "the universe root can be an Arabic path — NFC vs NFD is a live surface here". Concrete failure: a tab holding a cross-origin form (wikilink-resolved, session-restored, or NFC/NFD-divergent Arabic-root) of a referrer's path silently falls out of `targets` when the walker reports the note_links.source_path / disk-walk form — no adopt, no remount, no refusal, no conflict. No correction channel exists: the cascade:rewrote listener calls the same function with the same raw match; the watcher never sees cascade writes (watcher_suppress::was_recent) and adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs skips isCascading paths anyway. The next user edit in that tab debounce-saves the FULL stale body via writeNote → write_note with expect: None ("absent on legacy callers → unchecked"), writing [[Old]] back over the walker's [[New]] with journaled success, after which the detached reindex conforms the index to the reverted disk. Silent source-of-truth divergence with zero surfaced error — the exact BUG-015 F2 post-cascade-stomp class this reload exists to prevent. MED, not HIGH: the common-case forms match (tree/indexer/walker all derive from Rust PathBuf enumeration), damage is bounded to wikilink spellings in one open referrer, and the rename's always-stamped alias keeps the reverted [[Old]] links resolving.

confirmed_findings.summary: Focus-mode saves (commitFocusSave :1794) and the sidebar task toggle (:9866) broadcast screen:note-saved only 'if (secondScreenOpen)', but the SS window is HIDDEN, never destroyed (lib.rs:739-745 hide-on-close), and keeps its openTabs + note models alive; reopening the SS (handleToggleSecondScreen :5856-5874) re-emits only editorPanels and never re-syncs the SS's retained tabs from disk.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: SS is open showing note A in its tab strip; user closes the SS (window hides, tabs/models retained). In the main window the user edits A in Focus mode for ten minutes — every focus save skips the broadcast (secondScreenOpen=false) and the write is watcher-suppressed, so the SS's model of A never adopts. User reopens the SS: its still-mounted tab of A renders the ten-minutes-old body with no cue and nothing left to refresh it (no future broadcast fires unless the user edits A again in NotePane). Same-window NoteEditor saves broadcast unconditionally (NoteEditor.svelte:266/:320/:441), so the gate is drift between siblings, not policy.
confirmed_findings.reason: Every link verified in source: (1) commitFocusSave (+layout.svelte:1794) and the sidebar task toggle (:9866) gate broadcastNoteSaved on secondScreenOpen, while sibling save sites broadcast unconditionally (NoteEditor.svelte:266/:320, store.ts:652 nav_flush, :1868 prop_save, :6181 merge_resolve) — the gate is sibling drift, not policy. (2) Both SS close paths hide, never destroy (lib.rs:739-745 X-close, :297-302 close_second_screen), and both set secondScreenOpen=false in main (+layout.svelte:3939-3940 via onScreenClosed, :5852 toggle), so the gate is false exactly while the SS webview retains its openTabs and note models (cleared only on universe switch/workspace restore, SecondScreenPage.svelte:730/:841). (3) No other channel reaches the hidden SS: the focus save's disk write goes through gate_write, which marks watcher_suppress Rust-side (write_gate.rs:256-257) so 'library-changed' never fires for the app's own write, and the announce bypass covers only frontmatter bulk-ops and template writes — adoptFreshDiskIntoSS (SecondScreenPage.svelte:610) is reachable only from the never-fired screen:note-saved, cascade:rewrote, or watcher events. (4) Reopen (+layout.svelte:5856-5874) re-emits only editorPanels; the SS's retained tab of the focus-edited note renders its stale model with no cue and no remaining refresh hook. Silent, trivially reachable display divergence on a knowledge surface. Severity stays MED, not higher: ssReadOnly=true always (SecondScreenPage.svelte:208; NoteEditor.svelte:285 readOnly guard) plus setDisplayOnlyWindow(), so the stale model can never write back to disk; disk, FTS index (reindexNote runs per focus save), and the main window remain correct — the divergence heals on the next unconditional-broadcast save of that note, which the focus-only scenario never produces.

confirmed_findings.summary: The editor-panels sync $effect (:721-748) and split-companion $effect (:769-787) send content: $activeTab.content / t.content — but under SINGLE_OWNERSHIP handleSave never updates the store tab's content (NoteEditor.svelte:284-339 has no ct.content write; store comment store.ts:1888 'Do NOT update the store during autosave'), so tab.content is frozen at the last flush/open. Each re-fire of the effect (any openTabs/activeTabId store emission re-runs it) re-sends that stale snapshot, and the SS's u18 handler (SecondScreenPage.svelte:938-950) replaces editorPanelsData wholesale — overwriting the fresher content the SS just read from disk in its screen:note-saved handler (:676-686).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Cockpit active on the SS; user stays on note A in main and types 500 words. Debounced save lands → SS re-reads disk and shows the new text. Any subsequent openTabs store update that doesn't flush A (a background tab's watcher adopt bumping reloadVersion, closing another tab, a highlight update) re-fires the main $effect, which re-emits editorPanels with content = A's open-time tab.content — the cockpit's content-driven lens silently REVERTS to the 500-words-ago text on screen 2, no error, until the next save broadcast flips it forward again. Opening the SS mid-session (:5872 sends tab.content) starts it stale the same way.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in code. (1) Store tab.content is frozen under SINGLE_OWNERSHIP: NoteEditor.handleSave (:284-339) writes only to the model (editBody→saveNoteSession); saveTabContent explicitly skips the store (store.ts:1888 comment); flushOutgoing writes disk only; updateTabContent (store.ts:2958) has zero call sites; switchTab (:3916) only sets activeTabId. (2) The +layout $effect (:721-748) sends content: $activeTab.content (:737) and re-fires on ANY openTabs emission — activeTab is derived([openTabs, activeTabId]) (store.ts:1938) and legacy-store safe_equals semantics always invalidate object values — including emissions unrelated to the active note: tab pin toggle (+layout:302), closing another tab, watcher adopt into a background tab (store.ts:3705). (3) SS u18 (SecondScreenPage:938-950) replaces editorPanelsData wholesale, clobbering the fresh disk content its own note-saved handler set at :683; the cockpit lenses and NoteGaugeDeck render from that content (SecondScreenPage:1227 → SecondScreenCockpit:62/:168-172 → NoteButterflyGraph:392). SS-open (+layout:5866-5873) sends the same frozen snapshot. Recipe: type 500 words on A → save lands → SS re-reads disk (fresh) → pin/close any other tab → effect re-emits open-time content → cockpit silently reverts to the old text and stays stale until the NEXT save of A (indefinitely if the user is done typing). No error surfaced. Severity capped at MED: the cockpit is read-only (ck-ro; displayOnlyWindow guard store.ts:688 blocks SS flushes), so it is silent display↔disk divergence with no write-back or source-of-truth loss, and backlinks/outgoing self-heal via IPC.

confirmed_findings.summary: parseFrontmatter extracts the key as the raw line text including its quotes (`line.substring(0, colonIdx).trim()` — no unquote/decode), while classifyDoc (yamlDoc.ts:118) and composeFrontmatter's CST lookup (findItemIndex resolves the scalar) use the UNQUOTED key. For a quoted top-level key (`"reading list":` or `'date created':`) the projection key is '"reading list"' but the classifier/CST answer to 'reading list' — breaking the PJ-252 one-classifier invariant. shapes.get(key) misses, so the key falls into the unparseable-YAML fallback branch even though the doc parsed, and on write findItem/findItemIndex return -1.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: An imported note (python-yaml/Templater output quotes keys containing spaces or specials) has `"reading list":` with block items. User edits that row in PropertyEditor: compose's SET path cannot find the CST item (resolved key 'reading list' !== projected key '"reading list"'), so the splice is a no-op and serializeLine APPENDS a second key `'"reading list"':` — the file now durably carries two near-identical keys, the original untouched and a quoted-quoted twin, with the panel showing success. Deleting the row is worse: removeProp succeeds in the model, the CST splice misses, the save reports clean — the key silently survives on disk and resurrects on reopen. No error at any point.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: store.ts parseFrontmatter (line 2607) takes the key as raw line text with quotes intact (unquote/decodeQuotedScalar are applied only to values, lines 2752-2753), while classifyDoc (yamlDoc.ts:118) keys the shapes map by the resolved scalar String(k.value) — unquoted. For a quoted top-level key ("reading list": with a - alpha/- beta block) shapes.get('"reading list"') misses, so the key falls into the if(!shape) unparseable-YAML fallback (store.ts:2688) despite a clean parse, projecting an EDITABLE list row keyed with quotes — the PJ-252 one-classifier invariant is broken. The path is live: openModel (noteModel.ts:207/217) seeds props and base.props from this projection and composeModel (186) feeds composeFrontmatter; frontmatterIsRewritable is true so no refusal fires. Inside composeFrontmatter every CST lookup goes through findItemIndex, which compares CST.resolveAsScalar(k).value ('reading list') against the projected key ('"reading list"') and returns -1. Editing the row therefore skips the splice and APPENDS serializeLine's output — yamlStringify emits a distinct valid key '"reading list"': — leaving the file durably carrying the untouched original plus a quoted-quoted twin, with the save reporting success and reopen parsing cleanly (different key strings, no duplicate-key H1 trip). Deleting the row is a silent no-op: the REMOVE loop's findItemIndex misses, the block is re-emitted verbatim, the model goes clean, and the key resurrects on reopen. Input is reachable: PyYAML/Templater/exporter frontmatter quotes keys with spaces or reserved words, and Obsidian import is a first-class use case. Severity stays MED, not higher, because the original bytes are never destroyed (the splice always misses) and an untouched quoted key produces no diff and round-trips byte-perfect — the defect is silent durable divergence (duplicate twin key, failed delete), not loss of existing content.

confirmed_findings.summary: exportComposition hand-builds the new note's frontmatter by string concatenation — `title: "${compositionTitle.trim()}"` — without escaping embedded double quotes (and without quoteIfNeeded, the exported one-quoter PJ-187 mandates for every emitted frontmatter line; buildFullContent is imported at line 4 and never used). A title containing a double quote produces invalid YAML in the newborn note with no error.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User composes an expression titled `The "Living Link" Argument` and exports. The written note begins `title: "The "Living Link" Argument"` — a YAML parse error. The note is created and indexed with no complaint, but it is born with unparseable frontmatter: every future property intent on it is refused (tag adds, stage, dates — open path shows the banner with no hint why; closed path is finding #1's silent drop), composeFrontmatter runs in permanent H1 passthrough, and the Rust index reader's line-scanner may misread the title. Silent at the moment of corruption; the note is broken from birth.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at src/lib/components/ExpressionForge.svelte:139 — `exportComposition` emits `title: "${compositionTitle.trim()}"` by raw string concatenation. Only the fileName (line 136) is sanitized; the frontmatter title is interpolated unescaped, and `buildFullContent` is imported at line 4 but never called. The PJ-187 one-quoter mandate is real: store.ts:2802-2805 exports `quoteIfNeeded` precisely because "two other places were hand-building a `key: value` frontmatter line by concatenation and emitting invalid YAML" — ExpressionForge is a third such site the sweep missed. Reachability: Expression Forge opens from the command palette (+layout.svelte:2571); the title is a free-text input (line 158) with no character restriction, and the trail-import auto-title also flows in unguarded. I executed the exact emitted frontmatter against the project's own `yaml` dependency: a title of `The "Living Link" Argument` yields 1 parse error (UNEXPECTED_TOKEN at line 2 col 14) and the title decodes truncated as `"The "`. Silence: the write succeeds (writeNote takes the string verbatim), reindexNote runs, onClose fires — no error is possible at the corruption moment because nothing validates the YAML. Downstream mechanics claimed by the candidate are real in code: yamlDoc.ts:172/395 puts the note in H1 passthrough on parse errors, and noteModel.ts (PJ-207 §15, lines 329/366/382/400/426) refuses every future property intent on unparseable YAML — the open-note path later shows a could-not-be-saved banner with no hint of the birth defect, and non-panel paths refuse silently. This is a real, reachable, silent content-corruption: a note born with invalid frontmatter from a legitimate title.

confirmed_findings.summary: migrate_legacy_data writes over an EXISTING universe at the target path with no exists-guard: fs::copy(vaults.json) clobbers .constellation/libraries.json (line 1989) and a fresh meta with children:[] is fs::write-truncated over universe.json (line 2021, also non-atomic), then Ok is returned and the universe is activated. Its sibling link_library_as_universe had this exact defect and was fixed (PJ-207 §15, lines 1390-1419: !exists() guards + atomic_write); migrate_legacy_data never adopted the guard.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Machine state: app_data_dir has legacy vaults.json and NO universes.json registry (a pre-migration install, or app-data wiped by a reinstall), so check_migration_needed()==true and UniverseSetup routes handleNext to migrateLegacyData(name, folderPath+'/'+name). The user names it after a universe that ALREADY exists at that location (e.g. a modern universe synced there from another machine — the natural name to type). create_universe refuses when the directory exists; migrate_legacy_data does not check: create_dir_all succeeds on the existing .constellation/, the legacy vaults.json is copied OVER the universe's libraries.json (every library registration replaced by the legacy list), and a brand-new universe.json with children:[] and today's created date is truncate-written over the real one — the cUniverse federation manifest is gone. The federation links and library registrations are silently lost; the fs::write is additionally non-atomic, so a crash mid-write leaves a partial universe.json that later loaders surface as a parse error on a file the user never touched.

Returns Ok, writes a one-entry registry, activates the universe — no error, no backup. Reachability confirmed with a correction to the candidate: a full app-data wipe removes BOTH vaults.json and universes.json, so that branch does not arm the gate — but migrate_legacy_data never deletes vaults.json after migrating, so on any ex-legacy install the migration gate (check_migration_needed, line 1445) permanently re-arms whenever universes.json alone is lost; UniverseSetup.svelte then skips the welcome, railroads the user to name+location, and handleNext (line 109) calls migrate_legacy_data on folderPath+'/'+name — bypassing createUniverse's exists-refusal — so re-typing the same name/folder silently clobbers the real universe's library registrations and cUniverse federation manifest. The PJ-207 §15 fix comment in sibling link_library_as_universe (line 1395) even asserts migrate_legacy_data "has guarded the identical writes all along" — true only for the four default files, not libraries.json or universe.json. Silent manifest loss (libraries, federation, notes_folder), note content untouched → MED.

confirmed_findings.summary: run_one_safe's per-cataloger timeout is structurally ineffective: the worker runs inside std::thread::scope, and thread::scope JOINS all unjoined spawned threads before the scope returns. When rx.recv_timeout fires the Timeout arm, the abstain trail is constructed — but the scope cannot exit until the hung `c.classify(ctx)` actually returns. The V3-§8.r4.4 comment claims this fixed audit P1.4 ('a pathological regex in Structural or a hung embedding call in Semantic would block the IPC indefinitely'); for a genuinely non-terminating or long-blocked cataloger it does not — the timeout only converts a slow-but-terminating result into an abstain after the fact.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Semantic's embed path blocks on the shared embeddings engine mutex (wiring.rs:128) or a wedged ONNX session, or Structural hits a catastrophic-backtracking regex from data/cataloger_rules.json on an adversarial note body. The eprintln 'exceeded timeout — treating as silent' prints, then run_one_safe blocks anyway. If this happens inside the background scan (scan_job.rs run_scan → classifier_suggest_for_note), the scan thread stalls forever: progress stops mid-count with no error event, ScanState.running stays true so every later classifier_scan_start returns 'Scan already running' until app restart, and classify-on-open-note calls sharing the same wedged resource never resolve. No error surfaces to the user — the app just quietly stops classifying.
confirmed_findings.reason: The mechanism is real and provable from the code: run_one_safe (orchestrator.rs:153-195) spawns the worker inside std::thread::scope, whose documented contract joins all unjoined spawned threads before the scope returns. When recv_timeout fires the Timeout arm, the abstain trail is built but the scope still blocks until c.classify(ctx) returns — so the per-cataloger timeout bounds NO wall-clock time. The V3-§8.r4.4 comment ('recv_timeout enforces the per-cataloger budget', fixing audit P1.4) and Architect invariant 12 ('ensemble timeouts are bounded') are false guards. Worse, on every timeout the eventually-arriving real trail is silently discarded in favor of the abstain — full cost paid, result thrown away, suggestion quality degraded with no surfaced error. HOWEVER, the candidate's 'stalls forever until app restart' endpoint is refuted for today's wiring: Structural uses the Rust regex crate (linear-time — catastrophic backtracking impossible, structural.rs:27), Reasoning's LLM inference is wired None (abstains instantly, wiring.rs:76-79), and ONNX inference is CPU-bound with a 512-token cap — no non-terminating classify path exists. The concrete reachable failure is finite: constellation_embed_notes (embeddings.rs:429) holds the EmbeddingState.engine mutex across its ENTIRE batch loop (measured ~32s per large note; minutes for a batch), during which Semantic/Linguistic classify blocks at wiring.rs:128 for the full hold despite the 2s budget — the background scan silently stalls mid-count (running=true, no error event) then resumes, recording abstains. No lock-order inversion found (no path takes db-lock-held→engine-lock), so no permanent deadlock is constructible. Severity MED, not APP-KILLER: real silent freeze-class defect (minutes-scale stalls plus a load-bearing architect invariant that is a no-op), no source-of-truth loss, self-terminating today — but it becomes an indefinite-hang exposure the day the V3-§7.b LLM inference (or any network/hangable cataloger) is wired, because the protection everyone believes exists does nothing. Fix shape: replace the scoped join with a detached worker (Arc the cataloger and ctx, or move an owned clone) so the timeout arm can actually return, or document/enforce the budget at the blocking resources themselves.

confirmed_findings.summary: record_change silently returns when state.db is None (or the lock is poisoned, or ensure_ready fails), so the Tauri command record_shape_change (shape.rs:324) and apply_shape (shape.rs:204) report success while the shape_history row — which exists ONLY in search.db, like all earned data — is never written. No else, no log, no error.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Cold boot of the 7,820-note universe: tabs auto-restore instantly (MIG-100 reads disk, no DB needed) while init_db runs its 20-40s cold path. Within that window the user changes an open note's shape. The note model writes the frontmatter to disk (its own durable save, per MIG-101 §A-fix), then NoteEditor.svelte:605 fires record_shape_change → conn is None → record_change bails at shape.rs:239 → command returns Ok(()). The transition's from/to record existed only in that moment and is now gone; nothing can back-fill it. Later the user hits undo-shape: undo_shape (shape.rs:359) walks a history missing the step, hands back the wrong from_shape, and apply_shape writes that WRONG shape into the note's frontmatter — a user-gesture-driven wrong write with no error anywhere. Same hole fires mid universe-switch (invalidate_search_state nulls db).
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: record_change (shape.rs:235-241) silently returns on four conditions (no SearchState, poisoned lock, db=None, ensure_ready failure) and both callers report success — record_shape_change returns Ok(()) unconditionally (shape.rs:342) and apply_shape (shape.rs:204) records after the disk write, so set_note_shape/clear_note_shape also return Ok with no history row. The db=None window is real: SearchState::db starts as Mutex::new(None) (search.rs:1421) and is populated only by the frontend's async initSearchIndex() call after mount (+layout.svelte:4921/6224/6237); invalidate_search_state (search.rs:11228) re-nulls it on every universe switch. The shape gesture is reachable in that window — NoteEditor's ⋯ shapeScrap/shapePage/shapeClear (NoteEditor.svelte:669-677) needs only the tab and model, no readiness gate, and the record_shape_change invoke at line 605 is fire-and-forget whose .catch can never fire for this failure. The from/to pair exists only at gesture time and nothing back-fills shape_history, so the loss is permanent; a later Shape→Revert (undo_shape, shape.rs:359) consumes a stale row and applyShape writes the wrong shape (or removes the key) into the note's frontmatter with no error — silently breaking the reversibility guarantee the module's own header names as its purpose. The NoteEditor comment calls the silence deliberate best-effort, but shape_history lives only in search.db (earned-data class) and drives a write-back gesture, so this is a genuine silent false-success on a system-of-record write path. Severity stays MED: shape is presentation/templating only — note body, index, and content are never corrupted; the harm is a silently incomplete undo trail plus one wrong, user-visible, hand-recoverable frontmatter value.

confirmed_findings.summary: reindex_notes_matching_text returns Ok(0) when state.db is None, and its only IPC caller reindex_arabic_overrides (arabic/overrides.rs:811-818) never calls ensure_search_db_ready — so an Arabic-override CRUD during the cold-boot/switch window persists the override JSON but silently skips the targeted FTS5 re-tokenization, and nothing ever re-runs it.

The window is real and deliberately interactive: SearchState.db starts None (search.rs:1421), invalidate_search_state re-Nones it on every universe switch (search.rs:11248), and boot_bundle.rs:69-73 documents the "20-40s cold init" during which the Batch-S async fix keeps the UI responsive; ensure_search_db_ready's init runs on a local conn so the db mutex sits free-with-None the whole time — the reindex skips instantly rather than blocking. add/remove_arabic_override need no DB (JSON + in-memory layer) so the override persists while re-tokenization silently doesn't. confirmed_findings.summary: No ordering between a folder move's detached DB-migrate tail and a subsequent delete_path's index purge on the same notes: both queue on the SearchState.db mutex (not FIFO), and if the delete's purge wins the lock, the move tail afterwards migrates the pre-move rows onto the now-deleted destination paths — trashed notes silently resurrected in note_meta/notes_fts at dead paths, both commands having returned Ok.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Move folder A → B: move_item returns Ok; move_item_db_tail computes its (old,new) pairs from a walk of B, then parks at search_state.db.lock() behind a long-held writer. User then deletes B (trash mode): delete_path snapshots B/* descendants, moves B into .trash on the filesystem (path locks only, no DB lock needed), and its purge loop's reindex_delete_note calls queue on the same mutex. When the writer releases, if the purge acquires first it deletes B/* rows — which don't exist (the rows are still at A/*, exact-path DELETE matches nothing) — and then the move tail acquires and migrates A/* → B/*: every deleted note's note_meta/notes_fts/note_links/review_schedule rows now live at B/* pointing at files sitting in .trash. The follow-up reindex no-ops (files gone). Deleted notes reappear in search, backlinks and the review queue at dead paths with no error anywhere; healed only by that universe's next boot reconcile.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, reachable, silent race. move_item detaches move_item_db_tail (libraries.rs:2722), which computes (old→new) pairs from a destination walk and then parks on the unbounded SearchState.db mutex (2764) — the code's own §B2-4 comment documents multi-second parks here as the observed reason for the detach. A subsequent delete_path on the moved folder takes only path locks for its fs step, snapshots descendants at the destination paths, and purges those exact paths (8490-8567); with the tail's migrate not yet run, rows still sit at the pre-move paths, so the exact-path DELETE matches zero rows and delete_path returns Ok. The tail then wins the lock and migrate_note_db_paths (1532-1546, which checks only source-row existence, never destination-file existence) moves every deleted note's note_meta/notes_fts/note_links/review_schedule rows onto paths now in .trash. The tail's follow-up reindex_single_note cannot heal it: index_note_impl returns Ok(Skipped) for a missing file (search.rs:7886-7888), logging nothing. Watcher is suppressed for gated ops (delete_path's own comment, 8488-8489) and .trash is excluded from all walkers, so deleted notes silently reappear in search/backlinks/review queue at dead paths until the universe's next boot reconcile — both commands having returned Ok, no surfaced error anywhere. A mirror ordering (delete's fs move winning before the tail's walk) strands the rows at the source paths with the same outcome. Severity stays LOW: the window needs writer-mutex contention spanning a move-then-delete on the same folder, note files are safe in .trash (no content loss), and boot reconcile heals the index — session-scoped ghost rows, not durable corruption.

The frontmatter alias append (update_frontmatter_title) is the only remaining net; if the user later edits the aliases list, external references to 'Foo' stop resolving and there is no record the durable alias row was ever lost.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at libraries.rs:1865 — the 'rename' alias stamp is the one statement in the rename tail still `let _ =`-swallowed after PJ-149 made every migrate_note_db_paths failure visible (the `run` closure, lines 1575-1587); START/END tail lines log unconditionally, so an isolated INSERT failure leaves a clean-reading diagnostics.log. The silent path is reachable (transient SQLITE_FULL/IO error on this one statement that clears before Step 6). Real swallowed write, genuinely silent in a narrow window, redundancy-net loss only — LOW. Fix: route line 1865 through the same log-on-Err shape migrate_note_db_paths uses.

confirmed_findings.summary: The rename title-collision gate (resolveTitleCollision, MIG-099 §6 skip_stem=true) is a pure note_meta index seek with no disk fallback for own libraries — a note that exists on disk but is missing/stale in the index (the measured drift class: 60/7,824 drifted, 798 never-indexed found by PJ-207) is invisible to the check.

User renames another note TO 'Foo'; the index-only collision check returns null, the dialog that exists solely to prevent duplicate titles never opens, and the cascade then rewrites every [[Old]] referrer to [[Foo]] — a title that now names two different notes. Wikilink resolution silently picks one of them from then on; the user's links are re-pointed at an ambiguous (possibly wrong) note with no warning at any point.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: resolve_title_collision (libraries.rs:3059) runs resolve_in_library with skip_stem=true, which skips the filesystem stem walk and treats an empty note_meta/note_aliases index result as AUTHORITATIVE for own libraries (libraries.rs:3160 'trust the index result (even empty) — no filesystem scan'). The stat-guard (line 3155) only protects the index→disk direction; a note present on disk but absent from the index (the PJ-207-measured drift class: 60 drifted + 798 never-indexed of 7,824) is invisible. Because wikilink RESOLUTION keeps the stem stage (skip_stem=false, filesystem walk), a canonical-filename renamed note (path-stable) loses stem resolution to the unindexed Foo.md — the rewritten links silently resolve to the WRONG note, and a later index repair cannot undo the on-disk rewrite. Preconditions are a coincidence (specific drifted note + exact-title rename, cross-folder), so LOW stands. The create call site (+layout.svelte:4740) shares the same shape — fix both per the Whole-Ecosystem Fix Law.

confirmed_findings.summary: Three durable dirty-content flush sites omit the screen:note-saved broadcast their siblings carry: cid_ensure_flush (:3668), rename_flush (:4816), move_flush (:4975) — navFlushEnv (:647-664) exists precisely because 'a bare flush... would leave... the second screen un-notified', yet these three use bare standardSaveEnv with no onSaved.

The second screen has the same note open in a tab (or cockpit-focused): it goes on displaying the OLD disk content with no event ever telling it the file changed, until the user happens to type in that note again. rename_flush/move_flush lose only the last <1.5s of typing the same silent way before a rename/move.

The rename_flush (:4816) and move_flush (:4975) halves are real: a note typed into and renamed/moved within 1.5s gets its newest keystrokes durably flushed via bare standardSaveEnv with no screen:note-saved broadcast; the gated rename/move is watcher-suppressed (libraries.rs:1742, :8488), cascade:rewrote carries only referrer paths, and the second screen's rename/move handlers repath without content refresh (SecondScreenPage.svelte:145 explicitly defers content refresh to screen:note-saved, which never arrives) — so a second-screen view of that note silently shows stale content until the note's next save. The navFlushEnv comment (:642-645) itself names rename_flush as a bare flush leaving "the second screen un-notified"; flushAllTabsInLibrary was converted for this in the 2026-08-01 inspection and these siblings were missed. However, the candidate's headline cid_ensure_flush scenario is REFUTED: pendingCidEnsure admits only paths whose restore content lacks a cid_cn (store.ts:3775), and net-recovered content is identityProven and always carries one (:3687-3693) — a recovered tab never reaches drainCidEnsure; its dirty branch also reindexes (:3677) and any user-typed dirty content is broadcast by editor_save/editor_flush before a later activation. Impact everywhere is display-only: the second screen is strictly read-only (ssReadOnly=true, setDisplayOnlyWindow, SecondScreenPage.svelte:205-213), so no write-back, no disk or index divergence (rename_item_db_tail reindexes from current disk). Bounded to ≤1.5s of typing plus a frontmatter title line, self-healing at the next save or re-open — silent but small and transient, matching LOW.

confirmed_findings.summary: review_schedule.stratum for a note B is never refreshed when a link edit in ANOTHER note A changes B's sky stratum: maintain_sky_after_save (search.rs:2706-2726) and recompute_after_link_status_change (search.rs:11023-11063) update sky_nodes.stratum for the affected targets but never touch B's review_schedule row, and upsert_schedule_row only runs inside B's own index_note (search.rs:8320-8329). recompute_all_in (review.rs:1446) — the only heal, whose own doc-comment at review.rs:1390-1392 names exactly this drift — runs only from the repair tail / crash-marker converge, never in steady state.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User saves note A adding a 6th distinct inbound link to note B (B crosses a stratum threshold). sky_nodes.stratum for B is correctly recomputed by maintain_sky_after_save, but review_schedule.stratum for B keeps its old value. The Reviewer's due list sorts stratum-first (review.rs:496) and displays rs.stratum per row (review.rs:235/269), so B is silently ranked and labeled with a stale stratum indefinitely — until B itself is re-saved or the user runs an index repair, neither of which may ever happen for a note the user links to but no longer edits. No error anywhere; two derived surfaces (Sky View and Reviewer) permanently disagree about the same note. Partially acknowledged in code comments as repair-healed drift; reported because the heal is not reachable in normal operation.

The sole heal, recompute_all_in (whose doc at review.rs:1392 names exactly this drift), runs only from the repair tail (after_repair_run, search.rs:12111) and the crash-marker heal (heal_interrupted_walk via derived_heal::maybe_schedule, which is a documented no-op on every ordinary launch) — the doc's 'periodic reconcile' does not exist, and per converge.rs:411 the drift check cannot see a derived table stale against itself, so the repair door never opens for it. Result: after a save of A pushes B across a stratum threshold, sky_nodes.stratum and review_schedule.stratum disagree about B indefinitely with no surfaced error — the index-divergence class. However, the candidate's user-visible scenario is overstated: ReviewerView.svelte never renders stratum and priorities.ts has zero stratum references — the frontend re-sorts every lens by effective priority, overriding the backend's stratum-first 'stable initial order' (review.rs:493–496), and ReviewStatusPanel has no stratum either. The stale value is persisted and shipped in the DueNote payload but consumed by nothing the user currently sees, so the confirmed defect is the silent persisted two-table divergence itself (a latent landmine for any future stratum consumer), not a visible mis-ranking. LOW stands as the correct severity — real and silent, but with no user-visible consequence today.

confirmed_findings.summary: Within one save, index_note writes the note's review_schedule row from sky_nodes.stratum BEFORE that stratum is recomputed: upsert_schedule_row reads CAST(stratum) at search.rs:8321-8328, which executes before the note_links rebuild later in the same transaction (search.rs:8383+) and before maintain_sky_after_save runs post-commit in reindex_single_note (search.rs:12764-12768). The review row therefore always captures the PREVIOUS save's stratum — a permanent one-save lag between review_schedule.stratum and sky_nodes.stratum for the edited note.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User adds a 3rd outgoing link to note N and saves (a stratum +1 signal). index_note upserts N's review_schedule row using the pre-edit sky stratum, COMMITs, and only then does maintain_sky_after_save recompute sky_nodes.stratum to the new value. The Reviewer shows and orders N by the stale stratum until N's NEXT save re-reads the (by then current) value; a note edited once and then left idle sits one stratum step behind in the Reviewer with no error and no heal outside a full repair. Same user-visible surface as the neighbour-edit candidate but a distinct mechanism (write-ordering inside the save path rather than a missing cross-note hook); hooking review-row stratum refresh into the sky maintenance would fix both.
confirmed_findings.reason: Code-verified: index_note reads sky_nodes.stratum into review_schedule (search.rs:8320-8329) inside the save transaction, before the note_links rebuild (8383+); sky_nodes.stratum is only recomputed post-COMMIT by maintain_sky_after_save (reindex_single_note, search.rs:12764-12768), which updates sky_nodes only (2717-2724) and never the review row. Per-edge sky triggers are dropped (§B4, search.rs:2747), so the review row structurally always captures the PREVIOUS save's stratum. The divergence is user-visible and silent: the Reviewer pulse reads rs.stratum (review.rs:235, 310) — no live join — displays it per item, and sorts the queue by it (review.rs:493-496). No intermediate heal: ✓ Reviewed's DO UPDATE excludes stratum (review.rs:1249-1251), derived_heal fires only on crash markers, and review::recompute_all_in (which does fix it, review.rs:1390-1393) is reachable only via the ConvergeKey repair/reconcile door — not periodic. Severity stays LOW: both tables are derived (source of truth intact, fully recomputable), stratum is not an input to due-date computation (compute_schedule_row takes last_reviewed/interval/is_checkpoint/anchor only) so no note is wrongly due/not-due — the impact is a one-step-stale stratum in Reviewer display/ordering for a recently-edited then-idle note, healing on that note's next save or any repair. Fix direction the candidate names is right: refresh the review row's stratum inside maintain_sky_after_save, which also fixes the sibling neighbour-edit drift.

confirmed_findings.summary: The type dropdown is rendered on every row, including a structured ikhtilāf (nested-object-list) row. confirmed_findings.summary: migrate_legacy_data's bases copy discards every per-file error with fs::copy(..).ok() (and read_dir itself is inside if let Ok), so bases that fail to copy are silently absent from the migrated universe while the command returns Ok.

The migration completes, returns the new UniverseEntry, and the setup flow reports success.
